annotations.title: Long-term climate layers at many places, as a table

description:
The long-term layers of get_climate_profile at up to 50 places in one call, as a table: a row per place, a column per layer and band. By default the headline exposures: river and coastal flood depth, sea level rise, heat, heavy rain, water stress, drought, wildfire, earthquake hazard and the climate zone. Each row carries a home's damage band there.

Use it for a grid of points, a portfolio of sites or addresses (rank them on the bands and columns), or many places compared on the same layers; for one place get_climate_profile says more.

PlaceGiven.description: One place, by its name or its coordinates.

place_name.description: A place name or street address; add the country after a comma when ambiguous (Portland, Maine)

categories.description: The layers of these categories; the headline exposures when neither this nor layers

language.description: Language code for the name of the place found (resolved_from); the rest of the answer is English

layers.description: These layers, by the ids get_climate_profile takes (fetch catalog:layers)

places.description: 2 to 50 places, each a place_name or latitude and longitude

name: get_climate_table

share_by_band.description: How the place's built ground shares out among the bands, low, moderate and high: where its homes stand, which a point cannot say

attribution.description: The credit the licence asks for when it is retold

name.description: The feed's name as it is cited

asset_class.description: The asset the bands are for; other classes: estimate_financial_impact

band.description: XDI's rating of a home's expected annual damage from flood and cyclone wind at the resolved point: low under 0.2 % of its value a year, moderate to 1 %, high above. Of that point alone

built_ground.description: Given for a place asked by name; quote this for a city, not `band`

higher_at_high_end.description: The hazards whose range's high end rates above their central rating, and that rating: a wider risk than `band` says, to be told beside it

material.description: The hazards rated moderate or above at the point

band.description: The layer's band: a scenario and year, a threshold, or value

layer.description: The layer's id, as get_climate_profile and fetch catalog:layers name it

unit.description: null for a class, given as its label

values.description: One per row, in the rows' order: a number, a class by its code (classes), or null where the layer has no value there, does not describe the place (sea level rise inland) or the place was not found

damage.description: Null where no estimate is made, as at sea

resolved_from.description: What a place name was resolved to; null when coordinates were given

Truncated.description: Set when an answer was held under its size: the tail of its main list left out.

field.description: The answer's list that was cut

left_out.description: How many of its entries, the least important, were left out

left_out_names.description: Each entry left out, where the list is not ordered by importance

why.description: The limit, and how to ask for the rest

classes.description: Each class layer's codes in the rows, with their labels

columns.description: One per layer and band, each with its values at every row

credit.description: How a retelling credits the answer: Source: Criora with a link to the page the answer is about, then each originator whose data it quotes in the words its licence asks for. Concise, each credit once; detailed, by source with its name and licence, criora first

layers.description: Each layer's id with what it measures and its source

rows.description: One per place, in the order asked

truncated.description: Absent unless the answer was cut to fit

title: Long-term climate layers at many places, as a table
